rules.title: Ewes: pre-lambing clostridial (CD&T) vaccination window
rules.guidance: Ewes are typically vaccinated 3 to 4 weeks before lambing so antibody levels peak when colostrum is produced, passing protection to the lambs. Enter the expected lambing date to see this window.
rules.caveat: Some extension sources give a slightly wider 4 to 6 week window. Confirm the program and product with your veterinarian and follow the label.

rules.title: Lambs: start clostridial (CD&T) vaccination series
rules.guidance: Lambs' first clostridial vaccination is commonly given somewhere between about 2 and 5 weeks of age depending on whether their mothers were vaccinated before lambing; a booster follows a few weeks later, and all vaccinations should be finished at least 2 weeks before weaning.
rules.caveat: The right start age depends on the ewes' vaccination status, which this calendar does not know. Your veterinarian sets the actual schedule.

rules.title: Lambs: weaning (early-weaning system)
rules.guidance: In an early-weaning system lambs are weaned at roughly 60 days old and at least about 45 pounds, after being started on solid feed and water at least 2 weeks earlier. Lambs left with their mothers on pasture are naturally weaned much later, at around 4 to 6 months.
rules.caveat: Weaning age depends on your production system and lamb weight, not the calendar alone.
